scope_note: Amazon review logs only (about 8 discovery, 7 older holdout and 4-5 fresh). Nothing here says what the half-life in days is for other kinds of logs.

hypotheses.name: forget in days, not in rounds
hypotheses.statement: On Amazon review logs, a half-life fixed at 534 days (about 1.5 years) gives a better list than a half-life of 2 rounds when the log is cut into rounds of a different length (20, 45, 60 or 90 rounds instead of 30).
hypotheses.prediction: Holds at 60 and 90 rounds (2 rounds is then far shorter than 1.5 years) and probably at 20 rounds; no difference at 30 rounds, where 2 rounds is already about 1.5 years.

hypotheses.name: forgetting in days never hurts
hypotheses.statement: On Amazon review logs, the 534-day half-life loses less than 0.01 NDCG against 2 rounds at every round length tested.

gates.unit: Everything is judged SEPARATELY for each n (people per round) on the logs eligible at that n; at least min_logs_per_n logs are required, otherwise that n is 'not testable'. A missing expected cell makes the whole stage INCOMPLETE (no verdict).
gates.screen: n = 30 and 100, 6 draws, own draws. Keep a hypothesis if its primary rule moves the right way at any tested n: superiority mean diff > +0.005; noninferiority mean diff > -0.01; dominated mean diff < -0.005.
gates.full: PASS at an n: superiority = mean diff >= +0.01 AND diff>0 in >=70% of logs AND one-sided t lower bound at level alpha/(family*3) > 0; noninferiority = t lower bound of mean diff > -0.01 AND worst log diff > -0.03; dominated = mean diff <= -0.01 AND diff<0 in >=70% of logs AND t upper bound < 0. A hypothesis advances if it PASSES at one or more n.
gates.holdout: same rule at level alpha/3 for each n, plus the mean diff on the fresh logs alone must have the same sign (superiority > 0; noninferiority > -0.01; dominated < 0). CONFIRMED only at the n values that PASS both discovery and holdout.

designed_after: Generation 3 follows the generation-1 calendar check (H8: at 90 rounds the days-based half-life beat the rounds-based one in 9 of 11 logs; 3 of 4 fresh logs within 0.005 of best). The number 534 days is the median of the Amazon half-lives found in the earlier tracking study on the old discovery and holdout logs, so only the 4 or 5 fresh Amazon categories are blind to it. The family size counts all 12 hypotheses tried so far. Only Amazon logs are used because the days value is Amazon-specific (Gowalla is about 83 days).
